name: Druid
summary: Across Kalimdor, Druid protect the wild and heal the wounded with nature’s power. They draw on wild spirits, the celestial bodies, and the Emerald Dream, and take beast forms to defend the land. Night elves have followed this path for ages, tauren have renewed it, and the Skyborne keep their own traditions.

sections.title: Wardens of the Wilds
sections.body: Druidism binds its followers to nature and to the demigod Cenarius. Druids call up roots to hold their foes, draw power from the moon and stars, and use healing plants to mend bone and flesh. Their charge is to preserve the world’s balance and guard the wild from corruption and exploitation.

sections.title: The Gift of Shapeshifting
sections.body: Shapeshifting is the druid’s mark. Through spiritual devotion, druids channel the primal nature of Azeroth’s beasts. They take a bear’s thick hide to endure attacks, become lithe feline hunters to strike from shadow, or assume aquatic and avian forms to cross sea and sky. In animal form, their mouths rarely shape mortal words, yet their strength rivals the wild’s fiercest predators.

sections.title: The Cenarion Circle
sections.body: Cenarius taught Malfurion Stormrage the druidic arts ten thousand years ago. Later, the Cenarion Circle gave mortal druidism its order. From sacred Moonglade, it watches over druids across Kalimdor, apart from mortal factions and political disputes. For ages, only night elf men belonged, spending centuries in the Emerald Dream. After the Third War, night elf women and tauren joined them.

sections.title: Druids of the Skyborne
sections.body: The Skyborne learned druidism long ago. When common folk joined the Shal'nan's rebellion against Prince Tortheldrin in Eldre'Thalas, they took up nature magic, influenced by the Cenarion Circle to the north. Tortheldrin scorned the practice as beneath the Highborne. Their descendants still follow that path: the Nightclaw Druids of Shadowgale Forest on Zephras Isle remain largely apart from other Skyborne factions.

faq.q: Who was the first mortal druid?
faq.answer: Malfurion Stormrage was the first mortal to master druidic arts. He learned directly from the demigod Cenarius about ten thousand years ago, before the War of the Ancients.
Tauren learn the ways of the wild under Archdruid Hamuul Runetotem of Thunder Bluff. They now belong to the Cenarion Circle alongside the night elves.
The Cenarion Circle guides druids across Azeroth and protects nature. It stands apart from the Alliance and the Horde. Its members answer to the Circle’s archdruids and gather in sacred Moonglade.

faq.q: Can druids speak while in animal form?
aliases: can druids talk in bear form
faq.answer: Druids generally cannot speak normally in animal form because their voices reflect the beasts they have become. A few rare and exceptionally powerful druids have found magical ways around this limit.
The Emerald Dream mirrors Azeroth as it might be without civilization’s touch. Night elf druids have spent centuries asleep as they walk its paths and commune with nature’s spirits.

faq.q: Why were druids originally sleeping for centuries?
faq.answer: After the World Tree Nordrassil blessed them, night elf druids entered the Barrow Dens to wander the Emerald Dream for centuries. They aided Ysera’s green dragonflight in nurturing Azeroth’s spiritual ecosystem, until the Third War called them awake.
Night elves and tauren belong to the Cenarion Circle, while the Skyborne keep their own druidic traditions. The Nightclaw Druids live on Zephras Isle.

angles.text: For ten thousand years, kaldorei druids have guarded Kalimdor in quiet slumber. They keep nature’s balance under Malfurion Stormrage and the demigod Cenarius.
Under Archdruid Hamuul Runetotem, tauren have renewed an ancient bond with the wilds. They have joined the Cenarion Circle in sacred Moonglade and follow the path of the Earth Mother.
As a Druid, you guard the balance with animal strength, healing magic, and celestial power. You draw wisdom from Cenarius and the Emerald Dream.
As a Skyborne druid, you follow the path taken by Eldre'Thalas common folk during the Shal'nan's rebellion. The Nightclaw Druids of Shadowgale Forest still keep that tradition.
